directive.name: git
directive.description: Git workflow for festina lente tasks: committing and pushing on main. This directive owns ALL git operations. Skills have permission (allowed-tools) but no instructions to use git — this directive provides the instructions.

context.principle: All work happens on main. No feature branches by default.
All commits follow conventional commit format: type(scope): description
Implementation phase does not commit. Code stays uncommitted until finalize.

process.rule: Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
After updating project status to done, stage, commit, and push: - git add .festinalente/projects/{projectId}/project.xml - git commit -m "docs({projectId}): complete-project - {title}" - git push
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
After writing the spec and updated task file, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/spec.xml .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git commit -m "docs({id}): scope - {title}"
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
After writing the plan and updated task file, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/plan.xml .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git commit -m "docs({id}): plan - {title}"
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
Do NOT commit during implementation. Code stays uncommitted until the finalize phase.
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
Check for uncommitted changes: - Run: git status - Run: git diff --name-only If no changes found, warn the user and exit early (still update plan if needed).

Stage and commit all relevant files: - git add {changed files} - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/plan.xml - git commit -m "wip({id}): {progress summary}" The summary should briefly describe what was completed (e.g., "completed auth routes and login endpoint").
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.

After directive checks pass, check for uncommitted changes: - Run: git status - Run: git diff --name-only Display files that will be committed. If no changes found, warn the user and ask whether to proceed.

Determine commit type from the task's label using the commit-type field in workflow.yaml labels: - Label "bug" -> commit type "fix" - Label "feature" -> commit type "feat" - Label "docs" -> commit type "docs" - Label "refactor" -> commit type "refactor" - Default (no matching label) -> commit type "feat" Valid commit types are ONLY: feat, fix, refactor, docs.

Commit implementation: - git add {implementation files} - git add .festinalente/ - git commit -m "{commitType}({id}): {title}" ALWAYS include .festinalente/ files — they track task state and plan changes.
When a directive check fails and auto-fix is applied, commit the fix: - git add {changed files} - git commit -m "docs({id}): check-retry - {title}" Then restart all checks from the beginning.

After documentation updates are complete, commit docs: - git add .festinalente/product/ - git add .festinalente/engineering/ - git add .festinalente/glossary.yaml - If both product AND engineering docs updated: git commit -m "docs({id}): product+engineering - {summary}" - If only product docs updated: git commit -m "docs({id}): product - {summary}" - If only engineering docs updated: git commit -m "docs({id}): engineering - {summary}"
Update task status to "awaiting-completion", commit and push: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git commit -m "docs({id}): awaiting-completion - {title}" - git push
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
Update task status to "done", add completed date, commit and push: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git commit -m "docs({id}): done - {title}" - git push
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.

After updating the plan with the rework report and moving task back to in-progress, commit: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/plan.xml - git commit -m "docs({id}): rework - {title}"
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
After deleting the task folder, stage and commit: - git add -A .festinalente/tasks/{id}/ - git commit -m "docs({id}): delete - {title}"
Before starting, verify you are on the main (or master) branch: Run: git branch --show-current If NOT on main/master, output error and exit.
After implementation and user confirms commit: - git add . - git commit -m "quick({id}): {title}"
After updating quick.xml with completion details (status, files, commit, summary): - git add .festinalente/quick/{id}/quick.xml - git commit --amend --no-edit
If user requested doc updates and docs were changed: - git add .festinalente/product/ .festinalente/engineering/ .festinalente/quick/{id}/ - git commit --amend --no-edit

After creating product documentation files, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/product/ - git commit -m "docs: define-product - {brief product description}" Example: docs: define-product - task management app with projects, tasks, collaboration

After creating/updating product documentation and glossary, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/product/ - git add .festinalente/glossary.yaml - git commit -m "docs: map-product - {brief summary listing main features}" Example: docs: map-product - authentication, user management, notifications, search

After creating/updating engineering documentation and glossary, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/engineering/ - git add .festinalente/glossary.yaml - git commit -m "docs: map-engineering - {systems, patterns listed}" Example: docs: map-engineering - auth system, api system, middleware pattern
After creating the directive file and updating config.yaml, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/directives/{name}.xml .festinalente/config.yaml - git commit -m "docs: create directive - {name}"

check.item: Branch verification was performed at the start of the skill
All file changes were committed with correct message format
Commit messages follow conventional commit format: type(scope): description
No uncommitted changes remain after skill completion (unless implement phase)

example.code: # Correct commit messages: docs(022-add-dark-mode): create - Add dark mode toggle docs(022-add-dark-mode): scope - Add dark mode toggle docs(022-add-dark-mode): plan - Add dark mode toggle wip(022-add-dark-mode): completed toggle component and theme provider feat(022-add-dark-mode): Add dark mode toggle docs(022-add-dark-mode): product - complete dark mode documentation docs(022-add-dark-mode): awaiting-completion - Add dark mode toggle docs(022-add-dark-mode): done - Add dark mode toggle
example.explanation: Each phase has a specific commit format. The scope is the task ID, type matches the phase.

example.code:
# Commit type determination from task labels: # Task has label "bug" with commit-type "fix" in workflow.yaml # -> fix(001-fix-login): Fix login redirect bug
# Task has label "feature" with commit-type "feat" in workflow.yaml # -> feat(002-add-auth): Add user authentication
# Task has label "refactor" with commit-type "refactor" in workflow.yaml # -> refactor(003-cleanup-db): Simplify database queries
example.explanation: The commit type comes from the label's commit-type field in workflow.yaml, not from guessing.

example.code: # WRONG: Committing during implement phase git add src/auth.ts git commit -m "feat(001): partial implementation"
example.explanation: Implementation phase does NOT commit. Use /festina-save for WIP commits, or wait for /festina-finalize.

example.code: # WRONG: Using invented commit types git commit -m "festina(001): Add user authentication" git commit -m "task(001): Add user authentication" git commit -m "wip(001): Add user authentication" # wip is only for save phase
example.explanation: Valid finalize commit types are ONLY: feat, fix, refactor, docs. Derived from task label.
